To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Muslim women’s participation in aquatic activities in NZ is very low, 2) their participation in these activities is affected by the same social and environmental factors that impact on the participation of other women and men in NZ, 3) Muslim women’s experiences of aquatic leisure are shaped by their intersectional position as Muslim women, and 4) Muslim women’s leisure participation is affected by the way they are perceived by others, and by the way they perceive themselves.
The participation of Muslim women in aquatic leisure activities is limited.
